subject: RFP: Tenant fabric delineation and adversary scenarios review
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Tenant fabric delineation and adversary scenarios review

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our RFP assessment we need a concise statement of how Redwood partitions tenant traffic, plus a threat-oriented set of adversary scenarios that map to controls. Specifically, our security reviewers asked for:

1) A network diagram showing control plane vs. dataplane connectivity, any peering or transit hops, and where sidecar proxies live for tenant workloads.
2) A short description of your isolation model (network namespaces, security groups/NSGs, per-tenant VPCs, etc.) and how you avoid cross-tenant KV cache leakage.
3) Threat scenarios (3–5) showing likely adversary goals, attack paths, and which controls would block or detect them.
4) Any pen-test or canary test scheduling constraints, and whether you support customer-observed pen-tests (scoped).

Can you share a diagram and an attack matrix (even high-level) by end-of-day tomorrow? We will bundle this into our security evidence packet.

Thanks—
Ellen Park
Senior Security Engineer, Atwood Financial
ellen.park@atwood.com

[Attachment: RFP-scoping.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 10:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Tenant fabric delineation and adversary scenarios review

Ellen — attaching the diagram and a starter attack matrix per your request. High level answers up front, followed by attachments and next steps.

Summary (top-line):
- Isolation model: Tenant workloads are isolated at three layers: compute (K8s namespaces + runtime SELinux profiles), network (per-tenant subnets inside our VPC fabric with default-deny NSGs + Egress NAT per-tenant), and data (per-tenant encryption keys; optional HSM-backed keys for enterprise Private deployments).
- Control/data plane demarcation: Control plane components (orchestration, model registry, autoscaler) run in a dedicated management VPC with no inbound access from tenant subnets. Control plane communicates to tenant nodes over mTLS-authenticated control channels via an explicit service gateway; no direct SSH into tenant nodes.
- Sidecars & KV caches: Sidecar proxies run in the same pod boundary but enforce strict mTLS and token-bound cache namespaces. KV cache keys are prefixed with tenant IDs and validated at read time; cache eviction is tenant-scoped.
- Detection & telemetry: Per-tenant flow logs, token-level request traces (redacted prompt content), and model inference telemetry feed our anomaly detectors. All telemetry is retained per contract and available for audit.

Attachments included (see attached files):
- network-diagram-v3.png — shows VPC layout, transit gateways, service gateway for control plane, sidecar placement, and NAT/egress flow.
- attack-matrix-v1.xlsx — 5 mapped adversary goals, attack paths, mitigations, and detection hooks.
- evidence-packet-20270922.tar.gz — contains config snippets (SGs, example K8s NetworkPolicy), and sanitized audit logs.

Quick excerpts from the attack matrix (high level):
1) Goal: Cross-tenant data exfiltration via KV cache
   - Path: Compromise tenant app -> read cache keys -> exfiltrate via egress
   - Mitigations: tenant-prefixed keys, token-bound cache read checks, egress filtering, per-tenant KMS keys for sensitive caches
   - Detection: sudden multi-tenant cache read pattern, outbound anomalous transport

2) Goal: Control-plane coercion (mis-route workloads)
   - Path: Lateral move to control-plane interface from compromised node
   - Mitigations: control plane in isolated VPC, strict mutual TLS + mTLS client cert rotation, no inbound from tenant subnets; RBAC on orchestration APIs

3) Goal: Supply-chain (malicious model artifact)
   - Path: model push pipeline -> unvetted artifact accepted -> inference returns poisoned output
   - Mitigations: model signing, model provenance checks, canary traffic gating, signed rollout policies

Next steps we propose:
- We can host a 45-minute walk-through of the diagram and the attack matrix tomorrow morning (09/23).
- For pen-test: we support customer-observed scoped testing; procurement and legal signoff required. We use a pre-approved scope template for red-team activities (attached in evidence packet).

Let us know what additional telemetry or config snippets you need and whether you prefer the walkthrough to include our infra engineers (Ben) and the product security lead (Kimberly).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

[Attachments: network-diagram-v3.png (image/png), attack-matrix-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), evidence-packet-20270922.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: Tenant fabric delineation and adversary scenarios review

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the packet, very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after a first pass:

- HSM / Key separation: For Private deployments you mentioned optional HSM-backed keys. Can you clarify whether the control plane has any ability to unwrap tenant keys, or are they strictly customer-controlled? Also: do you support customer-supplied key material (BYOK) and rotation windows?
- Egress proof: We need a short statement on how egress flows are prevented from reaching arbitrary third-party destinations (we saw NAT per-tenant but want a policy statement + example SG/iptables snippet).
- Pen-test logistics: We usually run a 2-day focused pen-test on network + sidecar components. Are there blackout windows for your infra, and do you require an observability contact to be on-call?

Quoted for context: "On Wed, 22 Sep 2027 10:43:00 -07:00, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:"
> Summary (top-line):
> - Isolation model: Tenant workloads are isolated at three layers: compute (K8s namespaces + runtime SELinux profiles), network (per-tenant subnets inside our VPC fabric with default-deny NSGs + Egress NAT per-tenant), and data (per-tenant encryption keys; optional HSM-backed keys for enterprise Private deployments).

If you could provide short example snippets and a short declarative statement we can include in our evidence pack that would be ideal. Also please confirm whether you allow customer-run pen-tests against the sidecar layer (we prefer that).

Thanks,
Ellen
Atwood Financial Security

[Attachment: atwood-pen-test-scope.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atwood.com>, procurement@atwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Tenant fabric delineation and adversary scenarios review

Ellen / team — answering the follow-ups and proposing logistics:

HSM & BYOK:
- Statement: For Redwood Private we support two modes: (1) Redwood-managed KMS (Redwood holds ciphertext key-encryption-keys in our KMS, with role-based access controls), and (2) Customer-managed keys (BYOK) provisioned into a customer-controlled HSM or KMS. In BYOK mode the control plane never receives raw key material and cannot unwrap tenant data keys; cryptographic operations can be performed with HSM bindings or via a protocol that keeps keys inside customer HSMs. We will provide a key-usage attestation during onboarding.

Egress controls (policy statement + example):
- Statement: All tenant egress is routed through per-tenant NAT/egress gateways. Default-deny egress policies are enforced at the VPC edge; outbound allowlists are defined per-tenant and can be governed via procurement SLA. We provide example NetworkPolicy and iptables snippets in the evidence packet.
- Example (high level): iptables rules are generated from tenant allowlists and applied to the NAT instance. If an outbound destination is not allowlisted the packet is dropped and an alert is raised to the tenant and our SOC.

Pen-test logistics:
- We support customer-observed pen-tests against the sidecar and tenant application layer with pre-approved scope. We require a 72-hour notice and a signed scope. Blackout windows: we do not allow destructive tests against production inference runtimes during peak hours (we will share a standard blackout window schedule). Observability contact: yes — we ask customers to nominate a security contact and we provide an on-call Redwood engineer for the two testing days.

Operational next steps:
- Proposed walkthrough: 09/24 10:00–10:45 PT — diagram + matrix + short demo of per-tenant flow logs.
- I'll open a Jira (SEC-412) for evidence delivery and pen-test scheduling (link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SEC-412).
- We'll provide the sample iptables/NetworkPolicy snippets and an HSM attestation template by EOD.

If this works I'll send over the formal scope template and a DocuSign cover for the pen-test NDA.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
